findings.title: Backup code can be replayed due to non-atomic update
findings.body: In the backup code login branch, the code decrypts the stored backupCodes array, finds the matched code with indexOf, sets backupCodes[index] = null, and then updates the user record with the modified array. Because there is no transaction or conditional update (e.g., checking that the code is still present before writing), two concurrent login attempts using the same backup code can both pass the indexOf check and both write the modified array. This allows a single-use backup code to be used more than once, defeating its security purpose.

findings.title: onEnable not called if modal closed after successful enable
findings.body: After the TOTP code is verified, handleEnable sets the step to DisplayBackupCodes instead of calling onEnable. The onEnable callback is only invoked when the user clicks the 'Close' button in the backup codes step. If the user dismisses the modal by clicking outside, pressing Escape, or via the close X, the Dialog's onOpenChange fires but onEnable is never called. As a result, the parent component's state (e.g., the 2FA toggle switch) remains out of sync with the server, showing 2FA as disabled even though it has been successfully enabled.

findings.title: No end-to-end test for backup code login or disable
findings.body: The PR adds backup code functionality but the only e2e tests added verify the download, copy, and close actions on the backup codes screen. There is no test that actually logs in using a backup code or disables 2FA via a backup code, despite the PR description claiming these are supported. The TODO comment in the test file acknowledges this gap. Core authentication behavior with backup codes remains unverified by automated tests.

findings.title: Exported component is misnamed TwoFactor
findings.body: The default export of BackupCode.tsx is declared as `function TwoFactor({ center = true })`, which is a copy-paste error from the TOTP component. While it does not affect functionality, it is misleading and may cause confusion during maintenance or debugging.
